content.title: About
content.content: Lime juice is 100% freshly squeezed lime juice with no added sugar, preservatives, or water. It has a bright, tart flavor and the characteristic aroma of ripe limes, and is widely used in cooking, beverages, and cosmetics.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lime belongs to the citrus family and grows in tropical and subtropical regions.
A tablespoon (≈15 ml) of lime juice provides about 15 % of the daily recommended vitamin C.
Lime has been used in traditional medicine to aid digestion and as an antiseptic.
The acidity of lime juice can change the color of some foods, slowing the browning of avocado.
In several cultures lime is a symbol of hospitality and is used in welcoming rituals.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The acidity stimulates gastric juice production, helping to break down food.

items.title: Aids detoxification
items.content: Lime juice’s diuretic properties help the body eliminate toxins.

items.title: May reduce kidney stone risk
items.content: Citrus acids increase urinary citrate, which can inhibit formation of oxalate stones.

items.title: Improves skin health
items.content: Vitamin C and antioxidants combat signs of aging and promote healing of minor skin damage.

items.title: Acid reflux
items.content: People with high stomach acidity may experience increased heartburn after consuming lime juice.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may have an allergic reaction to lime.

items.title: Tooth enamel erosion
items.content: Frequent consumption of acidic drinks can wear down tooth enamel.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Lime acidity can affect the efficacy of certain drugs, such as anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add lime juice to cocktails, marinades, sauces, salads, and desserts. It is a key ingredient in guacamole, fish marinades, and as a refreshing addition to water or tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator in a tightly sealed bottle. Once opened, use within 5–7 days. Discard if the color, smell, or taste changes.
